title: First 90 Days: Ecosystem Mapping + Mentor Playlist (pilot)
body:
Purpose:
This short-play doc is a lightweight, practical template for pairing new hires with mentors and mapping the product/infra/inter-team ecosystem during the first 90 days. Goal is faster contextual ramp, fewer repeated questions, and measurable mentor impact. Pilot this with 6 hires (engineering + platform) in Q1 FY25.

Scope and principles:
- Focus: Ecosystem mapping (who owns what, critical services, common incidents), plus a 2-week mentor "playlist" of high-value activities that fit into normal mentor bandwidth.
- Minimal overhead: playlist items are 15–90 minutes each, scheduled across 14 days.
- Observable signals: checkpoints at day 7, 30, 60, 90. Collect 3 explicit success signals (handoff, small PR, customer-facing doc).
- Integration: ties into hiring plan (we'll flag hires who need cross-team mentors in interview loop) and onboarding checklist.

Outcome metrics (pilot):
- Time to first merged PR that touched a service (target: 14 days)
- Number of escalations to SRE from new hire in first 30 days (target: <=2)
- Mentor satisfaction (post-90d survey) and mentee-rated usefulness (NPS style).

Ecosystem mapping template (to be completed by mentor + new hire)
- Primary product area: (owner)
- Key services & owners: list top 6 with owner and runbook link
- Common debug paths: top 3 ways to root-cause customer issues
- Deployment cadence & release owners
- Monitoring & alerts: what alerts to ignore vs escalate
- On-call rotation and emergency contacts
- Developer tools & common dev env pain points
- Known technical debt that blocks quick wins

(Example: auth-service — owner: Priya N.; runbook: confluence/auth-service-runbook; debug path: logs -> trace-id -> db slow query -> missing index)

Mentor playlist (core 14-day sequence — adapt per role)
Day 0 (prework, async):
- Welcome message + access checklist validated (IAM, git, Slack channels) — mentor confirms
- Share topo map + quick diagram (15m reading)

Day 1–3:
- 30m: Walkthrough of product surface area (high-level) + where team contributes
- 45m: Show 2 live incidents from the past quarter and walk through RCA (read + 15m discuss)

Day 4–7:
- 60m paired setup: run a local end-to-end happy-path and create a tiny change (hello-world PR)
- 30m: Demo of CI/CD pipeline, where to check builds and flakiness signals

Checkpoint (end of week 1):
- Mentee: create a one-paragraph "service map" note and link to PR/branch created
- Mentor: quick async thumbs-up or 1:1 (15m)

Week 2 (days 8–14):
- 45m: Shadow on-call rotation (observe pager signal, no direct responsibility) or simulation walk-through
- 30m: Runbook editing exercise — fix a typo or clarify an ambiguous step (small doc PR)
- 60m: 1:1 alignment on first ticket/assignment and goal-setting to day 30

Manager & hiring-integration checkpoints:
- Add mentor recommendation to offer packet for hires flagged as "cross-team heavy" in interview stage.
- Interview rubric tweak: add a short question for candidates about past cross-team coordination; score 1–3.

Interview rubric snippet (people-ops suggested addition)
- Collaboration & context switching (1–4): examples of working across teams, how they approached ambiguity.
- Learning velocity (1–4): how fast candidate absorbs a new stack; probe with a brief follow-up question.
- Ownership (1–4): evidence of taking small end-to-end scope.
- Cultural fit (1–3): alignment with Redwood inference values (shipping, operational thinking).
- Quick guide to scoring: 12–15 = strong hire, 8–11 = hire with onboarding plan, <8 = consider further interviews.

Onboarding checklist (to cover in first 30 days; combine with existing corp checklist)
- accounts & access validated
- laptop provisioning checklist done
- basic security training completed
- first PR merged to non-trivial repo
- ecosystem map doc created and shared
- 1:1s scheduled for next 30 days (mentor, manager, 3 cross-team leads)
- join weekly team sync and intro in standup

Signals of success (examples)
- Week 2: created a PR and had it reviewed; wrote a small doc (runbook or README)
- Week 4: resolved or triaged a user-facing bug with owner handoff
- Month 2: presented a short "how things fit together" map in team demo
- Month 3: owns one small feature end-to-end or owns an on-call runbook update

Mentor guidance (short, do-able)
- Schedule no more than four 30–60m interactions in first 14 days; prefer async prep notes and a single focused pairing session.
- Use the playlist: tick items, add evidence links to the shared "ecosystem map" doc.
- Keep feedback concrete: one thing to stop/start/continue at each checkpoint.
- If mentor bandwidth limited: nominate a secondary buddy for tooling or CI help.

Templates (copy into candidate and onboarding packet)
- Slack: "@newhire welcome! I'm your mentor for first 90 days — quick note: I usually pair mornings MWF. Please ping me for pairing or questions. Short playlist: (link)."
- Manager handoff blurb: "New hire X — focus: infra onboarding, first 30-day goal: runbook PR + small service change. Mentor: Y. Cross-team checks: SRE, Platform."

Operational notes / dependencies
- Coordinate with infra and SRE to reserve a 1-hour "shadow pager" window each week for up to 2 mentees.
- Ensure access request turnaround SLA is <= 48 hours for pilot hires. Track outstanding access in a shared sheet.

Unresolved questions (to discuss with Ops lead)
- Do we tile this into the existing LMS (recommended) or keep as a living Google doc?
- Who owns measuring time-to-first-merge across org (eng metrics or people ops?)
- Do we provide a small mentor stipend for repeated pairings? Budget ask needed.

Pilot rollout plan (Q1 FY25)
- Week 0: finalize playlist & templates; update offer/emails (People Ops)
- Week 1–6: run pilot with 6 hires; collect survey at day 30 and 90
- Week 7: retro with mentors, hiring managers, SRE; iterate on playlist
- Week 8: decide scale vs retire pilot

Notes-to-self / scribbles:
- Keep playlist items short — mentors burn out if we ask for multi-hour blocks repeatedly.
- Try a micro-credential: "ecosystem-smarts" badge after evidence items completed.
- Potential follow-up: convert runbook-editing into a small hackathon for new hires every 6 weeks.

Linked materials (examples to copy/update):
- onboarding-access-checklist-template (Confluence link above)
- runbook-editing-guide (internal doc)
- hiring rubric matrix (HR drive)

If you want to pilot, reply to this doc comment or DM me in Slack (@aisha). Will schedule a 30m sync to align hiring managers and mentors.

-- Aisha P. (people ops)
